Taylor integral remainder gives jointly smooth signed-R Q_R=|zeta|^(2r)+R E in every specified finite norm.
Differentiating the smooth Taylor expansion gives rho=r^2|z|^(2r-2)(1+O(|z|)); the scaled curvature is positive near the unit circle.
The negative Cauchy projection is bounded on fixed finite Holder spaces by the cancellation kernel estimate and derivative commutation.
The fixed-circle map T uses f Q_zeta(f), without derivatives of the unknown h.
D_h T(v)=(r^2 conjugate(v-v(0)),2r^2 v(0)) is a bounded real isomorphism.
The Banach implicit-function theorem gives the normalized near-identity map in each fixed finite space.
The derivative stays within a fixed distance less than one of identity on the convex disk, proving injectivity.
Higher fixed-space branches agree by low-space uniqueness; no intersection of infinitely many parameter intervals is used.
Negative-mode cancellation and the real Stokes curvature integral force K(0)=0.
S_R=(r+K composed with inverse F_R)/zeta has only the prescribed residue and matches Q_zeta at the boundary.
Integrating S_R-r/zeta gives the logarithm-subtracted harmonic obstacle, normalized at zero.

A uniform collar, positive compact interior gap and dominating logarithmic term prove Q-U>0 throughout the hole.
First-order matching removes boundary measures; curvature is the positive pole atom inside and original positive curvature outside.
The removable subharmonic extension of any competitor minus the harmonic obstacle and the maximum principle identify the exact envelope.
The modified potential equals the original near the coordinate-chart boundary and defines a metric on the original L.

q->infinity absorbs the negative bump; m R^2->infinity, also for r=1, absorbs bounded Ricci curvature globally.

The continuous lower bound can avoid separated supports; shrinking collars and dominated weak limits cover accumulating exterior sources.

sqrt(q) R->0 is equivalent to q=o(m^(1/(r+1))); angular slope and the smooth volume/curvature ratios preserve the raw law.
